title: Rigveda 7.68: To Asvins
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.68: To Asvins: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.68 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Asvins. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 536v-537r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.68.1-5 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 5, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 536v
translation.original_text:
1ā śu̍bhrā yātam aśvinā̱ svaśvā̱ giro̍ dasrā jujuṣā̱ṇā yu̱vāko̍ḥ | ha̱vyāni̍ ca̱ prati̍bhṛtā vī̱taṁ na̍ḥ ||
2pra vā̱m andhā̍ṁsi̱ madyā̍ny asthu̱r ara̍ṁ gantaṁ ha̱viṣo̍ vī̱taye̍ me | ti̱ro a̱ryo hava̍nāni śru̱taṁ na̍ḥ ||
3pra vā̱ṁ ratho̱ mano̍javā iyarti ti̱ro rajā̍ṁsy aśvinā śa̱toti̍ḥ | a̱smabhya̍ṁ sūryāvasū iyā̱naḥ ||
4a̱yaṁ ha̱ yad vā̍ṁ deva̱yā u̱ adri̍r ū̱rdhvo viva̍kti soma̱sud yu̱vabhyā̍m | ā va̱lgū vipro̍ vavṛtīta ha̱vyaiḥ ||
5ci̱traṁ ha̱ yad vā̱m bhoja̍na̱ṁ nv asti̱ ny atra̍ye̱ mahi̍ṣvantaṁ yuyotam | yo vā̍m o̱māna̱ṁ dadha̍te pri̱yaḥ san ||
translation.text:
1COME, radiant Aṣvins, with your noble horses: accept your servant's hymns, ye Wonder-Workers: Enjoy oblations which we bring to greet you.
2The gladdening juices stand prepared before you: come quickly and partake of mine oblation. Pass by the calling of our foe and hear us.
3Your chariot with a hundred aids, O Aṣvins, beareth you swift as thought across the regions, Speeding to us, O ye whose wealth is Sûrya.
4What time this stone of yours, the Gods' adorer, upraised, sounds forth for you as Soma-presser, Let the priest bring you, Fair Ones, through oblations.
5The nourishment ye have is, truly, wondrous: ye gave thereof a quickening store to Atri, Who being dear to you, receives your favour.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 536v (numbered 57v by the scribe) (OPenn image 537, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.67.9 ‹bhūtam ye rāyā magha-deyam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 537r (numbered 58r by the scribe), begins in RV 7.68.6 ‹-jurate āśvinā bhūt cyavānāya›. Verses 7.68.1-5 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 7.68.6-9 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 5, varga 15); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 537r
translation.original_text:
6u̱ta tyad vā̍ṁ jura̱te a̍śvinā bhū̱c cyavā̍nāya pra̱tītya̍ṁ havi̱rde | adhi̱ yad varpa̍ i̱taū̍ti dha̱tthaḥ ||
7u̱ta tyam bhu̱jyum a̍śvinā̱ sakhā̍yo̱ madhye̍ jahur du̱revā̍saḥ samu̱dre | nir ī̍m parṣa̱d arā̍vā̱ yo yu̱vāku̍ḥ ||
8vṛkā̍ya ci̱j jasa̍mānāya śaktam u̱ta śru̍taṁ śa̱yave̍ hū̱yamā̍nā | yāv a̱ghnyām api̍nvatam a̱po na sta̱rya̍ṁ cic cha̱kty a̍śvinā̱ śacī̍bhiḥ ||
9e̱ṣa sya kā̱rur ja̍rate sū̱ktair agre̍ budhā̱na u̱ṣasā̍ṁ su̱manmā̍ | i̱ṣā taṁ va̍rdhad a̱ghnyā payo̍bhir yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
6That gift, which all may gain, ye gave Chyavâna, when he grew old, who offered you oblations, When ye bestowed on him enduring beauty.
7What time his wicked friends abandoned Bhujyu, O Aṣvins, in the middle of the ocean, Your horse delivered him, your faithful servant.
8Ye lent your aid to Vr̥ika when exhausted, and listened when invoked to Ṣayu's calling. Ye made the cow pour forth her milk like water, and, Aṣvins, strengthened with your strength the barren.
9With his fair hymns this singer, too, extols you, waking with glad thoughts at the break of morning. May the cow nourish him with milk to feed llim. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
